extraction.name: Visual Genome
extraction.description: A dataset of 108,249 images densely annotated with objects, attributes, relationships, region descriptions, and question-answer pairs to enable cognitive scene understanding.
extraction.creator: Ranjay Krishna, Yuke Zhu, Oliver Groth, Justin Johnson, Kenji Hata, Joshua Kravitz, Stephanie Chen, Yannis Kalantidis, Li-Jia Li, David A. Shamma, Michael S. Bernstein, Li Fei-Fei
extraction.citeAs: Ranjay Krishna, Yuke Zhu, Oliver Groth, Justin Johnson, Kenji Hata, Joshua Kravitz, Stephanie Chen, Yannis Kalantidis, Li-Jia Li, David A. Shamma, Michael S. Bernstein, Li Fei-Fei. Visual Genome: Connecting Language and Vision Using Crowdsourced Dense Image Annotations. 2016.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected and verified entirely by crowd workers from Amazon Mechanical Turk. The pipeline involved multiple task stages for each component (region descriptions, objects, attributes, relationships, region graphs, scene graphs, questions and answers).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 108,249 images from the intersection of the YFCC100M and MS-COCO datasets.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Canonicalization of objects, attributes, relationships, and noun phrases to WordNet synsets. Mapping involved using Stanford NLP tools, mapping to most frequent synset, hand-crafting rules for common failures, and verification by crowd workers.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For region descriptions, BLEU score thresholds (0.7) were used to ensure diversity and prevent repetition. For objects, Stanford's dependency parser was used to extract nouns as suggestions. For verification, majority voting (3 workers) and rapid judgments were used.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowd workers on Amazon Mechanical Turk drew bounding boxes and wrote descriptions for regions. They extracted objects, attributes, and relationships from descriptions. They wrote QA pairs (freeform and region-based). Verification involved majority voting (3 workers) or rapid judgments. Canonicalization involved mapping to WordNet synsets verified by workers.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Majority voting (3 unique workers) was used for verification. An annotation was added if at least 2 out of 3 verified it. Rapid judgments were used for objects. For canonicalization, workers verified mappings against 4 alternative synsets.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Average of 42 region descriptions, 21 objects, 18 attributes, 18 relationships, and 17 QA pairs per image.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 33,000 unique workers. 93.02% from United States. Majority between 25 and 34 years old. Youngest 18, oldest 68. 54.15% male, 45.85% female.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stanford NLP tools (dependency parser), Stanford CoreNLP, WordNet
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Enable the modeling of relationships and cognitive scene understanding. Potential applications include image search, question answering, and robotic interactions.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is somewhat biased towards images of people. Certain sports (skiing, surfboarding) are overrepresented due to a bias towards these sports in the image source. Common visual elements like 'blue sky' occur often. WordNet frequency counts bias canonicalization towards abstract senses over concrete/spatial senses.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Canonicalization mappings are not perfect and still contain some ambiguity. Current models are unable to reason about complex images (low accuracy in experiments). Region descriptions are short, causing models to fail to produce more descriptive phrases for regions with multiple objects.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and benchmarking for comprehensive scene understanding, cognitive tasks, image description, question answering, relationship extraction, semantic image retrieval, dense image captioning.
